cards.front: What should you know about good news?
cards.back: Unseen poetry tests skills, not knowledge. You can't revise the poems, so focus on developing analysis techniques.

cards.front: What should you know about form significance?
cards.back: Why did the poet choose this form? A sonnet about love connects to tradition. Free verse about trauma suggests breaking from conventions.

cards.front: What should you know about top tip?
cards.back: For unseen poetry, the 24-mark analysis question gets roughly 30 minutes and the 8-mark comparison gets 10-15 minutes. Always spend 5 minutes reading and annotating before writing anything — a well-planned 25-minute answer will always outperform a rushed 30-minute one.
Understanding (e.g. Show what the poem means; give personal response)
Analysis (e.g. Comment on language, form, structure)
14 lines, usually iambic pentameter (e.g. Love, serious topic, traditional)
Quatrains, ABCB rhyme, narrative (e.g. Storytelling, folk tradition)
No regular rhyme/meter (e.g. Modern, conversational, flexible)
Why does the poem break here? What shifts?
Are lines regular or varied? Why?
Where do lines run on? What flows?
Where do lines pause? What's emphasised?
Is there a pattern? Regular or irregular?

cards.front: What does Not annotating before writing mean?
cards.back: Always spend 5 mins reading and annotating
